summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and a history of anxiety was readmitted two days after discharge for recurrent nausea and vomiting. She presented with hypertensive crisis (BP 194/94) and lactic acidosis due to volume depletion, both of which improved with IV fluids and antihypertensive therapy. Throughout the hospitalization, she was observed inducing vomiting, leading to the recognition that her symptoms were primarily driven by a psychiatric condition. After discussions with GI and psychiatry, she acknowledged the psychological basis of her vomiting and committed to outpatient follow-up. Her diet was advanced, medications were optimized, and she was discharged home in stable condition with a plan for ongoing mental health support.
problems: Gastrointestinal malfunction arising from mental factors
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
Personal history of infections of the central nervous system
